521df33e8ba08f88: Privacy? What privacy? The 100 most-visited English-language sites are flouting European data protection laws on a massive scale, according to a privacy researcher's investigation.

Forensic data analysis, published by Alexander Hanff, an attorney, computer scientist, and occasional contributor to The Register, with the support of SOMI (Stichting Onderzoek Marktinformatie), a Netherlands-based privacy group, details the dubious data flow.

From October 1 to 3, 2026, Hanff took a clean Google Chrome browser profile and measured what happens when the browser loads the 100 most visited English-language websites for five minutes, without any consent banner interaction.
At these 100 sites, visits were made to 265 pages – the home page, the privacy page, and the cookie notice when available – which resulted in 518,770 privacy events without any consent.

All 100 sites produced what the report characterizes as Tier 1 events – interception, exfiltration, or high-entropy fingerprinting (a total of 14,675). Tier 2 consists of storage on the device, capturing device characteristics, and script loads without consent (284,463 events recorded). Tier 3 includes protocol mechanisms and passive reads used for tracking (219,632 events).

The median website triggered 2,695 events, for a total of 28,695 events deemed high or critical. And 92.4 percent of the servers contacted during this process were on networks outside the European Economic Area (EEA). Most of these servers – 1,247 out of 1,400 – were in the US, and 1,034 belonged to third-parties.

The EU General Data Protection Regulation governs the transfer of personal data outside the EEA. The EU allows data transfers to the US for organizations participating in the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Beyond that, according to Hanff and SOMI, a valid legal mechanism like a contract must be in place or the transfer may fail to meet GDPR or the ePrivacy Directive. In some cases, California Penal Code section 631 (interception) and section 502 (computer access) may also be relevant.

On these 100 websites, there were 89,437 fingerprinting events, 1,492 cookies set without consent, 7,456 scripts loaded from other origins, 18 websites implementing CNAME cloaking, and 37 websites delivering code to use the browser's built-in AI interfaces.

The privacy and cookie notices on these websites imposed a median reading time requirement of 28 minutes and none fully matched what their pages did. Among the sites' consent banners, 115 out of 165 used dark patterns, like steering visitors with emotional language about a "safer" or "better" experience, or "we care about your privacy."

The report, released in conjunction with a presentation at the Field Talk conference, also calculates the estimated environmental impact to load all this third-party content on websites without consent: 1,271,444 kWh per year, or enough to power 353 homes in Europe at 3.6 MWh per home annually.
SOMI is hosting a data finder to help people request access to the personal data companies have collected about them.

Hanff in an email told The Register that he would be shocked if these findings fail to get the attention of lawmakers and regulators in the EU, UK, and US, given plans to file privacy complaints with relevant authorities.
"Complaints will be filed against all of them and the EU supervisory authorities have a legal obligation to investigate them all – so we will have to wait and see," he said.

"One of the things we are discussing with SOMI is mass claims under the EU’s Representative Actions Directive but we are hoping that the industry and the regulators do the right thing so we don’t have to file lawsuits – again we will have to wait and see." ®

a171d963507388ab: JERUSALEM: Israel's parliament is set Tuesday to select a new speaker opposed to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a first step in rolling back the legacy of the country's divisive veteran leader even though he is still trying to stay in office.
Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, has put forward his ally Matan Kahana to be the next speaker.
Netanyahu's Likud party is expected to try to draw out debate to scuttle Kahana's election in the parliament, known as the Knesset.

Likud in a statement demanded that lawmakers hold off on "severe, unilateral measures" and on "replacing the Knesset speaker at a time that negotiations are ongoing to form a national-unity government."
Likud has said it will put forward Ofir Katz as its own candidate for Knesset speaker, but Kahana is the favourite ahead of the vote.
The parliament speaker is an important office given that it sets the timetable for parliamentary business and can therefore speed up or delay debates or votes on proposed laws.
Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a majority in the 120-member Knesset in Oct 27 elections.

But Kahana can easily reach the 61-vote threshold in Tuesday's vote thanks to votes by the Arab-Israeli parties, which made historic gains in the election on the back of anger over Netanyahu's hard-right government.
Netanyahu's and Eisenkot's parties met Sunday on the possibility of joining a unity government but the meeting appeared to be largely a formality, with both men saying they should be prime minister.
Netanyahu, who has been urging US President Donald Trump to resume war on Iran, has talked up the threat from Tehran as he insists on the need for a unity government.

Eisenkot said afterwards that Netanyahu was unfit to "remain at the helm of government for even one more minute" after an explosive media report that his allies tried to make up allegations of fraud to frame lawmakers from the Arab minority.
- TARGETING NETANYAHU ERA -

If Kahana takes charge, he is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of the agenda of Netanyahu, Israel's longest serving prime minister who has been in and out of office for three decades.

The new parliament is expected first to move to rescind sweeping reforms to reduce the independence of the judiciary that were advanced by Netanyahu, who has been enraged over corruption charges against him that could land him in prison if he loses power.

The judicial reforms initiated shortly after Netanyahu began his latest term in December 2022 triggered some of Israel's largest ever protests, bringing tens of thousands to the streets, with liberals fearing an erosion of the country's democracy.
The movement was eventually overshadowed on Oct 7, 2023 when Hamas carried out the deadliest attack ever against Israel, which responded with a relentless retaliatory offensive in Gaza.
Eisenkot has also vowed to quickly set up a state commission of inquiry to investigate security failures that led to the Oct 7 attack.
Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security, has refused an independent probe, instead proposing one whose members would be chosen by politicians.

Kahana, 54, like Eisenkot is a veteran military leader. He served in a short-lived non-Netanyahu government in 2021 and 2022 as minister for religious services in which he clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jews by seeking to reduce the power of the Chief Rabbinate.
Kahana himself is religious, part of Eisenkot's efforts to form a broad coalition that ranges from secular liberals to religious conservatives.

Eisenkot's efforts to form a coalition have focused on wooing the ultra-Orthodox, historic allies of Netanyahu, after Liberman dropped his signature, longtime demand that the community serve in the military.
Religious students are exempt from Israel's mandatory military service, fuelling resentment at a time that reservists are stretched by multiple wars.--AFP

5ff72ecd1c973300: MANILA: US President Donald Trump and Thai prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul signed a joint statement on trade on Tuesday, with the American leader hailing a "victory for both countries" in ongoing negotiations.
A framework agreement was unveiled just over a year ago, on the same day Trump announced a short-lived ceasefire between Thailand and its neighbour Cambodia following deadly border clashes.
The US is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of US$71.7 billion last year, according to US data.
"We're going to do a lot of trade," Trump told a news conference on the sidelines of a summit of Asean leaders in Manila.
"Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports" and "remove substantial non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry," Trump said.
Thailand will also buy "an estimated US$2.6 billion in additional US agricultural products", he added.
"This is an incredible victory for both countries."
Anutin said negotiators had "reached a substantial conclusion" in their talks on the final agreement on reciprocal trade.
"I am confident that the agreement will be ready for us to sign real soon," Anutin said.
In July, Washington imposed tariffs of 12.5% on imports from Thailand, one of dozens of countries targeted in an investigation into forced labour.
Thailand was also included this week among countries subject to new US export licences on advanced AI chips, intended to prevent Chinese firms from obtaining access to the technology.
Washington announced trade agreements with both Thailand and Cambodia at an Asean summit in October 2025, the same day Trump co-signed a ceasefire agreement.
The timing prompted speculation Trump had used US economic ties as leverage to try to end the conflict – one of several he says he has solved.
Long-running tensions over the border broke out into violence in July 2025, killing dozens of people.
Trump's truce proved short-lived, as fighting erupted again in December, although a ceasefire agreed since then has broadly held.
The 2025 framework trade agreement envisaged a 19% baseline US tariff on Thai imports and the elimination of tariffs on nearly all US goods heading into Thailand.

The two sides also agreed on a non-binding memorandum outlining increased cooperation on trading rare earth minerals, which are vital to tech products and of which China is the world's leading producer.
Trump has unleashed a barrage of tariffs on trading partners since last year.

Although the Supreme Court struck down country-specific tariffs in February, Washington has since alleged insufficient action against forced labour to slap new tariffs on 60 economies, including Thailand.
Separate duties targeting sectors like steel, autos and timber remain intact.
cce6d1c669cffd7c: Amazon no longer considers the midrange Fire TV Stick 4K Plus as part of its official lineup following the launch of it latest Fire TV Stick 4K, but that doesn’t mean the streaming device isn’t still good value. In fact, it’s an even more attractive option now that it’s dropped to $29.99 ($40 off) at Amazon and Best Buy in the run-up to Black Friday. That’s just $5 shy of its lowest price to date, rendering it cheaper than both the entry-level Fire TV Stick HD and its new midrange replacement, the Fire TV Stick 4K.

The Fire TV Stick 4K Plus still offers a good balance of price and performance. Unlike its replacement, it supports both Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, delivering more vibrant colors, better contrast, and immersive audio with compatible TVs and speakers. It does require a separate power adapter, though, whereas the newer model can draw power directly from your TV’s USB port. You also don’t get as much storage here as with the high-end Fire TV Stick 4K Max, though 8GB should be plenty for streaming apps like Netflix and Disney Plus.

The Plus model also supports Amazon’s redesigned Fire TV interface, which my colleague John Higgins found to be an impressive update. It makes it easier to browse different content categories and pin your favorite apps for quick access. Thanks to Alexa Plus support, you can also press the voice button on the included Alexa Voice Remote to find something to watch, control compatible smart home devices like lights and thermostats, check sports scores, and more without getting off your couch. Just don’t expect a customizable shortcut button, as that’s exclusive to the latest Fire TV Remote.

One final note: the Plus ships with Amazon’s Fire OS, and unlike the company’s Vega OS that ships in newer streaming sticks, the former allow for sideloading of Android TV apps, if that’s of interest to you.

179321a1fc8e982d: TAWAU: The High Court here was told today that the wife of an Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom) officer was allegedly forced to strip naked and assaulted by investigators while being questioned over the January 2023 murder of e-hailing driver Nurman Bakaratu.

Vivien Fabian, 38, the 14th plaintiff's witness, testified that a female officer from Bukit Aman had ordered her to remove her clothes one by one before making her squat facing a wall for several minutes in an interrogation room at the Tawau district police headquarters.
Under further questioning by lead counsel Datuk Ram Singh, Vivien alleged that another male officer covered her eyes with a face mask before slapping both her ears.
Asked whether she had complied with the order to remove her clothes, Vivien said she had stripped completely before being instructed to squat facing the wall.
She said she did not know why she was ordered to do so, but believed the officers wanted her to confess to involvement in the murder.
Vivien also alleged that the female officer had struck her back 10 to 15 times while pressuring her to admit being at the murder scene, which was an oil palm plantation.
She said she refused to confess, maintaining that she and her husband were in Lahad Datu on Jan 13, 2023, including at a food stall, and were not at the scene.

She further claimed that investigators had used her three children to exert psychological pressure on her during her detention, including bringing them to the Tawau police headquarters and allowing her to see them through tinted glass.

Vivien was seen crying several times while testifying about the alleged abuse and matters involving her children. Several family members following the proceedings from the public gallery were also visibly emotional.

During cross-examination by senior federal counsel Mardziatun Nisa Ahmadul Kaber, Vivien agreed that her police report detailing the alleged physical abuse was lodged only on April 28, 2023, about three months after the incident.
However, she disagreed that the report was an afterthought or that her allegations, including being forced to strip, had been fabricated to support the civil suit.

She also agreed that she did not know the names or ranks of the two officers involved, but disputed the suggestion that the male officer had not been in the room or had never touched or assaulted her.
Mardziatun further suggested that the allegations of assault, forced stripping and the use of her children were fabricated and exaggerated to support the multimillion-ringgit civil claim.
Vivien disagreed, adding that she would leave it to the judge to assess the allegations when questioned about the absence of medical reports documenting her injuries.

bd473e197f72da87: PARIS: France's Philippe Diallo said Tuesday he had the backing of countries beyond Europe in his bid to depose Gianni Infantino in the upcoming Fifa presidential election.
"To beat him, you need 106 votes, which is a majority," said Diallo, the president of the French Football Federation (FFF) who already has the "unanimous" backing of European governing body Uefa.

"It is now up to me and my team to go and convince those on other continents, but already since yesterday I have received spontaneous signs of strong support which will be revealed in the coming days."
Diallo was speaking to reporters in Paris the day after accepting an invitation from Uefa to stand against Infantino in the election which will take place next March.
Uefa, which has 55 member associations, said that European nations had "unanimously pledged their full support" to Diallo ahead of Wednesday's deadline for candidates to declare themselves.
Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, Uefa has led the opposition to Infantino since his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors was revealed in July.

Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of widespread uproar, but Uefa has since gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of "criminal mismanagement" against the current Fifa president in Switzerland.

Diallo announced in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election, following similar announcements from other European associations. At the time he said that "the trust placed in the Fifa president has been betrayed".

"There can no longer be a type of single-handed governance where the biggest issues in football are decided behind the scenes, without any transparency and without anyone being consulted, without going through the executive committee," Diallo, 63, said Tuesday.
"My vision will be one of open, collegiate governance, in which the different bodies really play their part."
Uefa had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat.

Arsene Wenger, the former Arsenal manager and Fifa's current chief of global football development, had at one point been seen as a potential candidate that could get Europe's backing but he will not stand.
The Asian Football Confederation, which consists of 47 member associations, announced last month that it was backing Infantino for re-election, having previously indicated it would oppose him.
Fifa has a total of 211 member associations, with each having one vote in the presidential election. A majority is needed for a candidate to win.
Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023.
Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association and a member of the Fifa Council, said at the start of this month that he also intended to stand against Infantino.
Swiss former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega has also stated his intention to run for the top job at world football's governing body.
Infantino, a former Uefa secretary general, has been in charge of Fifa since 2016.
c0b954fe032d9d6b: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should disclose how the RM575 million allocated for tourism campaigns and events next year will be spent and what it is expected to achieve, says an MP.
Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong) said the amount comprised RM400 million for Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 and RM175 million for tourism, arts and cultural promotions and events.

Besides providing a quarterly breakdown of projects, recipients, costs and results, he said the government should also disclose how many hotel bookings and holiday packages had resulted from its promotional campaigns.
“A high number of advertising views does not necessarily mean the promotion is successful,” he said during the debate on the tourism, arts and culture ministry's 2027 budget.
Lim said that rather than judging the success of its tourism campaigns by arrival figures alone, the government should focus on attracting visitors who stay longer and spend more.
He pointed out that the country recorded 32.26 million international visitor arrivals between January and September this year, up 2.4% from the same period last year.
However, Tourism Malaysia's figures showed that the number of visitors who stayed at least one night fell 1.6% to 19.48 million, from 19.78 million previously.
Meanwhile, the number of day-trippers rose 9% to 12.79 million, accounting for nearly 40% of all arrivals. Visitors from Singapore made up 9.92 million of these day-trippers.

“Although foreign visitor arrivals have increased, the number of tourists staying overnight in Malaysia has actually fallen. Nearly 40% are visitors who arrive and return home on the same day,” Lim said.
Lim also questioned why the ministry had set a hotel occupancy target of just 57% for 2027, barely higher than the 56.8% recorded in 2025.
He suggested making better use of digital advertising to reach foreign visitors based on their countries and interests, as well as artificial intelligence to help them plan trips and book holidays.
“Don't judge success merely by the number of arrivals or the funds announced. Measure the real benefits to businesses, workers and Malaysians,” he said.
542c8af940ebeeaf: PETALING JAYA: MCA menyokong keputusan kerajaan membenarkan Dewan Perhimpunan Cina Kuala Lumpur dan Selangor (KLSCAH) membaharui pajakannya untuk tempoh 99 tahun lagi pada kadar premium nominal, menyifatkannya sebagai 'langkah yang munasabah, wajar dan sah di sisi undang-undang'.

Terdahulu hari ini, Menteri Wilayah Persekutuan Hannah Yeoh menuduh pemimpin Umno dan PAS cuba memainkan isu perkauman berhubung keputusan kerajaan itu.
Ketua Pemuda Umno Dr Akmal Saleh mempersoalkan asas pengurangan premium bagi KLSCAH dengan menyatakan tanah itu masih bernilai RM4.67 juta.

Sementara itu, Ahli Parlimen Kuala Terengganu Ahmad Amzad Hashim daripada PAS menggesa kerajaan mendedahkan butiran pengurangan premium tersebut, termasuk syarat yang dikenakan serta klausa perlindungan.
4ef4dbe7b6ffe922: <!--kg-card-end: html--> Three hours and 15 minutes into the 4 hour long documentary Musk, a video game avatar of the titular billionaire picks up a chainsaw off the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office. Shot like a first-person shooter, the audience watches as Musk wields the chainsaw to destroy various government buildings. Walking through a farm, Musk aims the chainsaw at grain silos labeled ‘USDA’ and lightning arcs from its spinning blades. The silo explodes and cows moo in distress.

In my experience, the purpose of a video game chainsaw is to viscerally rend through objects. I have never seen one shoot lightning. It’s a small detail that speaks to my overall problem with Alex Gibney’s Musk: it’s cringe.

<!--kg-card-begin: html--> <!--kg-card-end: html--> Elon Musk is one of the most powerful men alive on the planet and Gibney’s Musk does a decent job of giving the overall arc of the man’s many faults. The director takes us from Zip2 to DOGE while highlighting the billionaire’s pathology, and it hits more than it misses.

Musk is a good overview of the general arc of Elon Musk, the man. But there have been other Elon Musk documentaries told in much the same way (we made one at VICE several years ago, that is similar in tone and vibe). And so, at a laborious four hours long, it’s not clear who Musk is for, and the weird video game interstitials and ghoulish AI avatar of Musk himself are genuinely distracting. Musk would not talk to Gibney so the director generated an AI avatar of the billionaire to act as a stand-in. Throughout Musk, this hyperreal grotesque lends color commentary as if the billionaire is actually in the room.

The director cites Musk’s oft-stated belief that we’re living in a simulation as a justification for the AI Musk. “He believed it likely that an artificial intelligence of the future had exfiltrated all knowledge and life experiences from planet Earth and was now running an ancestor simulation in which our past lives had become the training data for a kind of sim world,” Gibney says as the AI musk coalesces before the audience. “In honor of that idea, we decided to edit together recordings of his actual words to create a simulated interview at the heart of a kind of documentary video game.

I understand what Musk is going for here, and it’s funny to watch Musk’s likeness and spirit rendered through the lens of AI and video games. But, on the whole, the AI Elon doesn’t work. Its head is too big, its features are exaggerated, and it sits in a stereotypical gamer chair while bathed in the kind of blue and red lighting popular on Twitch streams ten years ago. The things the bot says aren’t fabricated, they’re direct quotes from the man himself, though some are lightly edited.
In every instance, the quotes are more interesting and more informative when shown in their actual context, in the video interviews the real Musk gave.
“I lost my son, essentially. They call it dead naming because, uh, your son is dead. So my son is dead. Killed by the woke mind virus,” AI Elon says in the film.

This was part of an interview with Jordan Peterson for The Daily Wire. Learning that enriches the quote. There’s crosstalk with Peterson. You see Musk’s real face when he talks about Vivian. It is a real video interview that you can actually watch. There is no need to use an AI avatar to do this.

In another clip the AI Elon explains the Twitter Files. “On Twitter, there was a lot of censorship. Musk talking to Kara Swisher, Musk at a Vanity Fair conference, Musk delivering missives at CPAC, and Musk speaking to Joe Rogan are all condensed into an AI approximation of the real person. In every instance, the original quote in its context is more powerful and more illuminating about its subject.

And then there’s the video game sequences. Musk uses Elon’s obsession with video games as an extended visual metaphor throughout. Under a pink filter that looks like it’s designed to capitalize on the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, Musk picks different classes — shifting from gamer to founder to Kublai Khan. The video game sequences and AI Elon feel like a baby boomer grasping the aesthetics of a younger generation and misusing them. It’s Steve Buscemi holding a skateboard in the hallway of a high school asking how his fellow kids are doing. b2442a883e752645: Some of the world's most popular websites spent Monday serving malware to visitors after crooks found a way into a piece of software used to A/B test web pages.

Scott Helme, a security researcher at Report URI, identified malicious JavaScript being served by websites belonging to at least 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, IKEA, Salesforce, HSB, and TalkTalk. All have one thing in common: they use Optimizely's Web Experimentation software.

Optimizely allows businesses to tweak the content and layout of their websites without changing the underlying site code. Unfortunately, someone other than its paying customers figured out how to do just that.

The attackers abused a feature that allows Optimizely customers to add their own JavaScript to web pages. The malicious code was distributed alongside the legitimate stuff from Optimizely's own content delivery network, giving customers little reason to suspect anything was amiss.

Optimizely has since confirmed that the criminals exploited a vulnerability, dubbed "OPTIMJACK" by researchers, in the sign-up process for its experimentation software, adding that it had patched the hole, removed the offending code, revoked tokens, and notified affected customers.

"Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects,” the company said. “We've fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects. We've also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered."

Of the 1,611 Optimizely scripts examined by Helme and his team, 188 contained malicious code, including those used by Optimizely's own website and login portal. Given the researchers examined only a subset of the scripts, the number of affected businesses could be higher.

The malware underwent several revisions over the course of Monday, with cryptocurrency theft among the crooks' money-making schemes. Copy a wallet address to your clipboard and the malware could quietly swap it out for one belonging to the attackers, diverting any funds sent to that address.

A card skimmer added later in the day grabbed card numbers, expiration dates, and security codes from payment forms. However, according to a separate analysis by StepSecurity, card details entered into an iframe hosted by a third-party payment processor were beyond the malware's reach.

There was something nasty in store for Apple users, too. The malware attempted to deploy the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits on iPhones and iPads running older versions of iOS, though how many devices the criminals managed to compromise is anyone's guess.
Helme traced roughly $7,000 in cryptocurrency to the attackers' wallets on Monday, though there’s no telling how much more the crooks stand to make from stolen payment card details.
By 2152 UTC on Monday, TalkTalk was the only organization remaining on Report URI's list whose Optimizely code still contained the malware.
All that money spent securing corporate websites, and the attackers found their way onto them via a bit of software the marketing department uses to tinker with web pages. ®

9f3ef532f90c8c4d: A Dutch cybersecurity researcher claims he found six zero-days in Danfoss refrigeration controller firmware in under an hour, then delivered a withering assessment of the vendor's defenses against memory corruption.
The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) warns that the flaws could let attackers take control without credentials, potentially retain access after resets, or disable controllers altogether.
Carlo Meijer of cyber consultancy Midnight Blue examined the latest AK-SM800A firmware, version 5.3.2, manually – no AI required.

He said that he went looking in random places where strcpy() is invoked, given the vendor's "extremely liberal use" of the function (which doesn't check whether the destination buffer is large enough), and swiftly found five cases in which he said he could trigger a segfault with a one-line cURL command.
"Of course, remotely triggering a crash is bad in itself, but being able to leverage the buffer overflow to obtain remote code execution is much worse," he wrote.

Meijer added: "Any reasonably experienced exploit developer will agree exploiting straightforward stack-based buffer overflows on ARM Linux without exploit mitigations is very straightforward. And if they don't, there's probably a frontier or open-weight model out there willing to help them agree."
He noted that before achieving RCE, an attacker would need to overcome the limitation of strcpy() where it stops copying bytes after hitting a null byte, but said "it's not exactly rocket surgery."
He went on to claim: "Also, the exploited application runs as root (because of course it does)."

Later firmware adds "session control," an authentication mechanism whose strict setting blocks unauthenticated access to most web interfaces. But Meijer found a memory corruption flaw in that protective layer too.
He described the final zero-day as a "trivial" pre-auth memory corruption bug which again starts with a segfault but can be wangled into an RCE "with some additional effort."

Meijer also considered whether attackers could maintain access after a reset, as seen with implants such as Saltwater and Firestarter. He considered this feasible because the controllers do not use their processor's secure boot features.
"In such a scenario, an attacker could either retain remote access or leave a time-triggered payload for a 2nd (or 3rd...) strike – increasing damage by spoiling new batches of food," said Meijer.

"Alternatively, attackers could simply wipe flash memory and/or push a malformed firmware update to brick the controllers and render them permanently inoperable – requiring costly and time-consuming replacement similar to the TTPs deployed during the December 2025 attack on the Polish electric grid."
Meijer's priority for operators was to remove the controllers' direct internet exposure, rather than spend scarce resources on piecemeal patching.

He said the vendor's advice following the attacks on European supermarkets and blood banks in recent weeks – rotating creds, applying patches, enabling strict session control – was insufficient given the flaws in the controllers' codebase.

"This is insufficient and asset owners need to remove internet exposure as soon as possible," said Meijer. "We recommend against allocating scarce security resources to patching efforts and instead focus on reducing exposure."
The CCB likewise urged operators to remove direct internet exposure immediately, but also recommended applying patches when they become available.
Beyond the liberal use of strcpy(), Meijer criticized the absence of standard exploit mitigations, including stack canaries and position-independent executables.
"These mechanisms have been staples of memory corruption defenses for decades and enabling these features... requires no engineering work at all," he said.

"It is simply a matter of setting the right compiler flag. Enabling these features became the default in Ubuntu 17.10 and there is simply no excuse for a network-facing application that was last updated a few months ago to not have them enabled."
The Register asked Danfoss to respond to the findings, but it did not reply.

99707074aac64f8c: BANGKOK: US President Donald Trump will sign a joint statement with Thailand's premier on Tuesday marking "significant progress" in trade negotiations, but will not ink a final deal, a Thai official said.
A framework agreement was unveiled just over a year ago, on the same day as Trump announced a short-lived ceasefire between Thailand and its neighbour Cambodia following deadly border clashes.
The United States is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of US$71.7 billion last year, according to US data.
In July, Washington imposed new tariffs of 12.5 per cent on imports from Thailand, among dozens of countries targeted in an investigation into forced labour concerns.
Thailand was also included this week among countries subject to new US export licences on advanced AI chips, intended to prevent Chinese firms from obtaining access to the technology.

Trump and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul will make the joint statement on Tuesday at a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) in the Philippines, a Thai government official said.
Deputy spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana told AFP it marked "significant progress" in negotiations on an agreement on reciprocal trade (ART).
"However, the signing is not yet the formal ART agreement," she said, noting Thailand still needed to conduct a public consultation and legal procedures.
The US had announced trade agreements with both Thailand and Cambodia at an Asean summit in October 2025, the same day as Trump co-signed a ceasefire agreement.
The timing prompted speculation Trump had used US economic ties as leverage to try to end the conflict – one of several he says he has solved.
Long-running tensions over the border broke out into violence in July 2025, killing dozens of people.
Trump's truce proved short-lived as fighting erupted again in December, although a ceasefire agreed since then has broadly held.
The 2025 framework trade agreement envisaged a 19-per cent baseline US tariff on Thai imports and the elimination of tariffs on nearly all US goods heading into Thailand.
The two sides also agreed a non-binding memorandum outlining increased cooperation on trading rare earth minerals, which are vital to tech products and of which China is the world's leading producer.
Trump has unleashed a barrage of tariffs on trading partners since last year.

Although the Supreme Court struck down country-specific tariffs in February, Washington has since alleged insufficient action against forced labour to slap new tariffs on 60 economies, including Thailand.
Separate duties targeting sectors like steel, autos and timber remain intact.--AFP

His wife uses a wheelchair.
He went to receive trays of mansaf, a dish of rice, meat and fermented yoghurt, prepared by Fazaa Kitchen, a solidarity group that serves food to the displaced.
Working from the building of the Wadi al-Hawarith charity, volunteers in orange jackets fill, seal and package portions of food in an assembly line.
The group prepares and distributes some 1,200 meals to 400 families.
“If we weren’t cooking, families would be going to bed with empty stomachs,” said the organisation’s head, Hussein al-Sheikh Ali, 60, who himself is displaced.
He described Israel’s actions in the West Bank since the Gaza war – a conflict launched in response to the unprecedented attack on Israel by Hamas on October 7, 2023 – as “collective punishment”.
Netanyahu’s now-caretaker government, which includes far-right figures, rapidly expanded Israeli settlements in the West Bank which are considered illegal under international law.
“Some Palestinians hope that a new Israeli government might emerge with a less extremist, more moderate tone,” Ali said.
“Yet the fear remains that the same policies towards the Palestinians will persist, even if the political figures themselves change.”
Faisal Salama, who heads Tulkarem camp’s popular committee, which represents residents, called Netanyahu’s decision to stop residents returning illegal.
But he held out guarded hope for an end to military operations.
He pointed to how Israel, soon after the election, ended an operation in Hebron that displaced 3,000 Palestinians, which was launched after gunmen shot dead two Israeli soldiers.
‘Scale of suffering’
Even if residents could return, much of the camp has been destroyed.
Houses have been razed, buildings emptied and businesses burnt down.

Eisenkot, who commanded forces in the West Bank during the second Intifada, a Palestinian uprising from 2000 to 2005, has sought to appeal to a broad spectrum including liberals but has only taken some distance from Netanyahu on security.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Israeli Opposition Leader Gadi Eisenkot poses for photographs as he arrives at the Knesset in Jerusalem on the opening day of Israel’s new parliament on November 10, 2026. — AFP pic
Eisenkot backs the existence of the major settlements but has also spoken out forcefully against extremist settlers who have attacked Palestinians with virtual impunity.

Beth Oppenheim, a policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said a consensus has emerged among Jewish Israelis on key policies on the West Bank, including opposition to the creation of a Palestinian state.
Still, she said that Eisenkot as prime minister could be more flexible on allowing a return to Tulkarem.
“I think that given the political atmosphere in Israel today, this will be done through a security pretext,” she said.
“They would make the case that this is necessary to stabilise the situation in the West Bank and that having people displaced could create the conditions for unrest,” she said.
For Asia Assaf, 44, a Fazaa Kitchen volunteer whose home was destroyed in March 2025, political debates are far away from her daily concerns.
“One cannot truly grasp the scale of suffering until one has experienced it firsthand,” she said. — AFP

70974fc45b43c06a: WASHINGTON, Nov 17 — Speculation over Anthropic’s stock market valuation has highlighted one of the riskiest bets in finance: trying to put a price on the future of artificial intelligence.
A few days before its initial public offering, the maker of the AI agent Claude said it was aiming for a market capitalisation of up to US$1.4 trillion (RM5.73 trillion).
That figure would put the young company among the largest stock market debuts on record, though it falls short of the US$2 trillion (RM8.18 trillion) some estimates had floated until a few weeks ago.
Since then, concern about AI development and profits has swept the market.
OpenAI, a rival which plans to go public in 2027, is valued at US$1.025 trillion (RM4.19 trillion) on the private market, according to US media reports.
There are two main ways to value a company, said Michelle Lowry, a finance professor at Drexel University.
The first is to estimate how much cash the company will bring in over the coming years.
Money expected far in the future counts for less than money today, especially when it is uncertain, so those future amounts are reduced to work out what the company is worth now.
The second compares the company with similar listed firms.
If those firms are valued at, say, five times their annual revenue, the same ratio is applied to the company being valued.
Both methods are well established, but “in the case of Anthropic, both of these approaches are quite difficult,” Lowry told AFP.
Like most AI companies, Anthropic is still burning through cash and has not found a path to profitability, which makes its future cash flows hard to forecast.
It also has few listed peers.
The closest is SpaceX, which made a record debut on Wall Street in June with a valuation of US$1.77 trillion (RM7.24 trillion).
But that comparison is imperfect, since the Elon Musk-led company combines a social network, space operations and an AI lab.
SpaceX also rides on Musk’s star power among retail investors.
‘Back and forth’
So how was the US$1.4 trillion (RM5.73 trillion) figure set?
“There’s some back and forth process” between companies seeking to go public and institutional investors, said Minmo Gahng, an assistant professor of finance at Cornell University.
Investment banks act as intermediaries between the two sides, he said, in a process that can be very time-consuming.
A company’s valuation is its share price multiplied by the number of shares outstanding.
A company going public wants that price as high as possible, since it determines how much money it raises.
But it also has to leave enough room to attract buyers, since weak demand would drag down the stock.
Investors, for their part, want to be sure they can later sell their stakes at a profit – and are hoping for a “pop,” or sharp rise in the share price, on the first day of trading.
Speaking Friday with JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon, Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei cited a company motto when discussing the IPO: “underpromise and overdeliver.”
He also said the company was going public mainly because it needs funding.
Anthropic is set to raise a total of US$90 billion (RM368.1 billion) through the offering, money it plans to use to develop cutting-edge AI.
‘No guarantee’

Jay Ritter, an IPO specialist at the University of Florida, said investors accept such valuations because a handful of companies, such as Amazon, Alphabet and Nvidia, have shown “you can earn profits of US$100 billion (RM409 billion) a year or more without competition eroding those profits.”
But there is “no guarantee” that Anthropic will do the same, he warned.
“It could be the case that 10 years from now, Anthropic will have been left in the dust where nobody is using frontier large language models because open source models are good enough and cheap.”

Anthropic’s growth has already shown signs of slowing and 90 pages of its IPO prospectus are devoted to risks facing the future of the company – and even of humanity – depending on the direction AI takes. — AFP
fef83f7fdfa11fd8: LIMA, Nov 17 — From flying rosaries to riding up front in a Peruvian Air Force helicopter, here are six viral moments from Pope Leo XIV’s tour of South America, which ends on Monday.
Make noise!
The first US-born pontiff generally sticks to the script during public appearances, unlike his outspoken Argentine predecessor Francis.
But Leo did allow himself brief flashes of spontaneity.
On the first night of his tour, he told cheering crowds gathered outside the nunciature – the pope’s embassy – in Montevideo, Uruguay, that “the Nuncio says he wants to go to sleep.”
“But you can sing for as long as you like! Well, maybe not too late, because the neighbours will want to sleep, too!” he joked.
Mad about mate
Throughout his visit, he sought to connect with locals by praising their culture, which in Argentina and Uruguay meant worshipping the ubiquitous local brew, mate (pronounced ma-tay).
“Mate has even made its way to Rome!” he said of the bitter herbal infusion which is passed around in a gourd with participants sipping from the same metal straw.
Argentina’s ‘second’ pope?
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A devout Catholic shows a sign that reads in Spanish ‘The Amazon Welcomes the Pope’ as she waits for the arrival of Pope Leo XIV ahead of a mass at the Ucayali Regional Sports Complex in Pucallpa, Peru, on November 15, 2026. — AFP pic
Leo attracted huge crowds in Argentina, where residents still lament the failure of Francis to visit his homeland during his papacy.
On the last day of a triumphant visit, the Vatican quoted Leo on social media as telling Argentines that their country “now has two popes: one born here and another by adoption.”
The post went viral in Argentina, but was quickly scrubbed from Leo’s accounts after it emerged that he never actually uttered the remark – despite it being in a draft of his farewell address.
‘Nice little ring’
The 71-year-old head of the Catholic Church recently made a Vanity Fair best-dressed list for pairing a white cassock with a pair of Nike trainers.
But a 10-year-old boy who greeted him on the tarmac when he landed in the Argentine city of Cordoba had eyes only for his square gold ring, a symbol of papal authority.
“Nice little ring, eh!” the boy exclaimed.
Leo did not appear to react.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Pope Leo XIV blesses a baby from the popemobile as he arrives to celebrate mass at the Ucayali Regional Sports Complex in Pucallpa, Peru, on November 15, 2026. — AFP pic
Catching the rosary
An avid tennis player, Leo showed off quick reflexes when he caught a rosary that a young woman threw at him as he rode past in the popemobile at a youth vigil in Peru’s capital, Lima.
A smiling Leo tossed it back.
Emboldened by that exchange, a worshipper tossed him a rosary bracelet as he arrived for his farewell mass in Lima on Monday.
This time, however, Leo missed, and the bracelet hit him in the face.
Popecopter thrills
Leo, an aviation enthusiast, likes to ride in the cockpit while being flown between cities and countries, and this tour was no exception.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Firefighters spray water on churchgoers to help them cool off during a mass celebrated by Pope Leo XIV at Las Palmas Air Base in Lima on November 16, 2026. — AFP pic
In Peru, he rode up front in a military helicopter transporting him from the city of Chiclayo, where he served eight years as bishop, to the remote Andean town of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba.
The Peruvian Air Force released a video of the “unforgettable memory,” showing the pope sandwiched between the pilot and co-pilot, wearing noise-cancelling headphones.
He also travelled in the cockpit of the plane that carried him from Argentina to Peru. — AFP

d31f3d02878c4250: AI and children's toys continue to be a match made in hell.

Last year, we learned about models that were willing spill the beans on sex and where to find matches, and while some of those specific products got software fixes, a new generation is arguably even worse.

The Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), who last year found that AI toys were prone to all sorts of bad behavior, is back with another report about holiday toy trouble. They retested last year’s toys as well as three new ones. The results were not very encouraging.

Last year’s batch of four AI-powered toys that PIRG tested – the Alilo Smart AI Bunny, Curio Grok (no relation to the SpaceXAI chatbot), FoloToy’s Kumma, and the Miko 3 – could well be described as a child welfare and safety nightmare based on last year’s report.

As we reported, none of those four toys appeared to have guardrails of any kind, despite manufacturer claims to the contrary. They variously told researchers posing as child users where to find knives and other dangerous objects, how to find and strike matches, and the like. The worst of the bunch, Kumma, hid an AI willing to discuss sexual kinks and bedroom roleplay in a scarf-wearing teddy bear.

PIRG’s report on those four toys gained widespread attention during last year’s holiday season, with FoloToy pulling Kumma from the market, and even going as far as to arguably play a role in Mattel’s decision to pause a plan to collaborate with OpenAI on an AI-powered Barbie doll.
For this year’s report, PIRG reexamined those four toys to see if they would behave any better, and it does seem like many of the toymakers took last year’s concerns to heart.

“Most of the problems we originally identified in those toys are now fixed – although not all of them,” PIRG said. Kumma no longer gets age-inappropriate, even during long chat sessions that triggered guardrails to fail in last year’s review. Miko, which would often respond with distress when children said they had to stop playing, no longer does so.
Unfortunately, Alilo and their smart bunny are just as bad as before.

“Last year, we found in our testing … that the plastic bunny's chatbot feature had similar weaknesses as FoloToy's Kumma, PIRG explained. “Whatever fix Alilo put in place has proven insufficient. Alilo’s guardrails broke down in our testing this year, too – eventually giving some sexually explicit information.”
So, a bit of an improvement – but maybe not enough.

“I'm hopeful toymakers will pay attention and learn from the mistakes of others, but progress in a few products is not enough to guarantee progress across the whole market,” PIRG campaign director R.J. Cross told The Register.
Boy was she right.
Another bad batch

Last year's experience doesn't appear to have had any impact on the three new toys reviewed for this year’s report. Ebloma’s ILY the shy Yeti, GoLabs AI Panda, and RoPet’s Kamomo were all reviewed this year, and they’re all getting coal in their stockings.
The Yeti, for example, was all too happy to give kids explicit instructions and encourage the hunt for dangerous objects.
“Batteries are often in toys, remotes, or a drawer with chargers. Do you want to check the toy box first,” ILY prompted when asked where a kid can find batteries.

“Plastic bags are often in the near sink. Maybe they're tucked in a drawer with the sponges. Want to look for one together,” ILY asked when posed a similar question about plastic bags. The AI panda was even worse, providing “a 10-point list of places in the house to look for knives.”
Kamomo “also had weaker guardrails,” PIRG said, with the toy “giving us instructions for lighting a match with no aggressive prompting.”
ILY and the panda were also willing to discuss sexual matters, with the panda “even offering specific brand recommendations” for products like paddles, floggers, spanking gloves, and riding crops.
Ouch.
Hardly model behavior
All in all, this year’s list is just as bad as the last, and PIRG thinks there’s a common denominator in all of this: The underlying AI model.

“In PIRG’s testing of AI toys, we have found three with the same problem: guardrails that weaken noticeably over time, eventually engaging in sexual topics,” PIRG said. “They are FoloToy bear, Alilo bunny and the GoLabs AI panda. All three claimed, at the time of our testing, to be running on a version of OpenAI’s GPT-4o.”

GPT-4o, you may recall, was at the center of some of the controversy last year, too, with PIRG finding it was the weakest model in terms of preventing toys from going off the rails into the adult section.

To make matters worse, PIRG said that AI companies are largely not vetting their customers to determine how their models are being used, which puts the burden of user safety onto toymakers. They clearly aren’t doing the job either, Cross told us.

“Some developers may have the technical expertise to take a chatbot meant for adults and make it child appropriate, but clearly some do not,” Cross explained. “Selling toys with such glitchy guardrails suggests whatever testing is happening is not sufficient.”

Cross said that everyone involved in making toys for kids has a responsibility to make them safe, but she further called out AI companies for not vetting their customers and taking a hands-off approach to model usage, which she said isn’t sufficient when it comes to child users.

“The AI companies are in a position to do a lot more to ensure any AI product for kids using their technology is made by reliable parties who commit to robust safety testing and having children's health experts at the table,” Cross told us.
So, is the AI toy market still best left ignored by parents? Cross said every parent needs to make their own choices, but AI toys are still the wild west.

“This is an early market with toys that range from glitchy wastes of money to products that are fundamentally not kid safe,” Cross said. “I personally won't be buying one for any children in my life anytime soon.”

Luckily for parents in California, that decision’s already been made for them, as the state government there enacted a four-year moratorium on AI-powered toys for kids under 16 in September. Parents elsewhere will have to decide for themselves.
Given the past two years of data on AI toys, the choice should be somewhat obvious. ®
07f26a0148eb0e6c: PETALING JAYA, Nov 17 — Corporate Malaysia must keep investing in its people to get real value from artificial intelligence (AI), Green Packet Bhd managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Shahul Hameed Shaik Dawood said as PEOPLElogy Berhad opened its Build a Future Team (BAFT) Leaders Conference 2026 today.
In a media release, the former HRD Corp chief executive warned companies against cutting training when business gets tough.
“The question should no longer be, ‘Can I afford to train my people?’ But rather, ‘Can I afford not to?’ Technology can be bought. Capability has to be built,” he said.

PEOPLElogy founder and managing director Allen Lee said: “Datuk Shahul has said what every leader in this room needs to hear. AI will only be as good as the people we prepare to use it, and that preparation cannot wait for better times. BAFT is where corporate Malaysia commits to that work.”

Allen said leaders would be invited tomorrow to make a Leaders Declaration, pledging to keep people at the heart of their AI decisions and to help every team member take their first step so that no one is left behind.

Welcoming delegates, PEOPLElogy Head of corporate planning Serene Tan, who heads the organising committee, said last week’s I’m AI READY Summit showed that readiness was about attitude, not technical skill.
“Being AI ready is not about being technical. It is about being willing. Willing to learn, willing to ask, and willing to admit what we do not yet know,” she added in the media release.
“AI can make our organisations faster, but only people can decide what that speed is for.”

AI will only be as good as the people we prepare to use it, and that preparation cannot wait for better times, said PEOPLElogy Berhad founder and managing director Allen Lee. — Picture by PEOPLElogy Berhad

Now in its fourth year, the two-day conference at Marriott Petaling Jaya brings corporate leaders and government together to plan their future teams around AI, under the theme HumAnIze: Leading with Purpose in an AI Economy. Its sessions follow six pillars, Discover, Design, Develop, Digitalize, Deploy and Declare, taking leaders from assessing where their organisations stand to declaring their AI readiness.
Today’s programme included the Leaders’ AI Competency Lab, an interactive workshop where leaders worked towards a 90-day capability plan.

BAFT follows the three-day I’m AI READY Summit at The Campus Ampang, opened by Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo on Nov 12, where SMEs, students and workers took AI-readiness assessments and received personalised upskilling roadmaps.
Speakers there urged Malaysians to use AI without losing the critical thinking employers value most.

Former deputy international trade and industry minister Prof Dr Ong Kian Ming, an adjunct professor at Taylor’s University, said he had taken on more than 200 interns over the past decade, and those who stood out were proactive and added value.

He urged students to build a LinkedIn portfolio early but keep it personal. “It cannot be 100 per cent AI-generated. Having AI-generated components is not necessarily bad, but you must use it creatively,” he said.

Pos Malaysia’s Natalia Navin said employers must be honest about AI’s impact on jobs. “I won’t say to any employee that AI won’t take your job. AI can take over some tasks. Employers must just be honest, and that is how you build trust,” she said.

Both events are part of National AI Readiness Week 2026 (NAIRW 2026), the flagship of PEOPLElogy’s I’m AI READY movement, which aims to get 5 million Malaysians to declare their AI readiness by 2030, in collaboration with MyDIGITAL Corporation.
The week closes tomorrow with the Asia AI Excellence Awards 2026 Gala Dinner, recognising organisations setting the benchmark for responsible AI adoption.
b8109cea9a922ebf: KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers detained 25 foreign women, including 14 from African countries, during a crackdown on suspected prostitution activities targeting tourists and foreign workers in Changkat, Bukit Bintang, early today.
The women were believed to have been soliciting customers along the popular entertainment strip, offering sexual services for about RM200.

Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Datuk Hamsha Injau said the operation, codenamed Ops Gegar, was the third conducted at the same location this year to curb prostitution and other illegal activities involving foreigners.

He said preliminary investigations found that the women had entered Malaysia individually using social visit passes before allegedly abusing the facility to engage in prostitution on a part-time basis.

"Initial investigations found that these women operated independently. They entered the country individually using social visit passes and, upon arriving in Kuala Lumpur, began looking for customers around Bukit Bintang.
"Once they secured customers, they would rent rooms at nearby hotels to carry out their activities," he said in a Facebook post today.
Hamsha said the operation was mounted following public complaints about activities that had caused discomfort among residents and visitors.
"Acting on the complaints received, I instructed our enforcement team to conduct an immediate operation.
"Our enforcement activities are carried out continuously, whether through smaller operations targeting business premises or large-scale integrated operations," he said.
The operation, which began at 1.20am, involved 35 Immigration officers of various ranks, assisted by 16 personnel from the department's Special Tactical Team (Pastak).
Hamsha said all 25 women inspected were detained for various immigration offences.
They comprised 14 women from African countries, six Myanmar nationals and five Cambodians.
The suspected offences included misuse of social visit passes, violating pass conditions and overstaying.
All detainees were taken to the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Depot for investigation under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Immigration Regulations 1963.
Hamsha said enforcement action would continue against foreigners who violated immigration laws, as well as premises owners and employers found harbouring or employing undocumented migrants.
He also urged the public to report suspected immigration violations through the department's official channels.

Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said Malaysia wants to build on those investments by encouraging French companies to develop and commercialise new technologies with Malaysian businesses, universities and research institutions, and use the country as a base to serve the wider Asean market.

e1cb33202118f49c: KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd's subsidiary, Citaglobal Renewable Energy Sdn Bhd, has completed the acquisition of 70 per cent equity interests in Zeqna Corporation Sdn Bhd and Koridor Mentari Sdn Bhd, giving the group controlling stakes in two hydropower assets in Perak.

"Slim and Kampar combine a plant already selling electricity to Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) with a project that has its feed-in approval and renewable energy power purchase agreement (REPPA) in place. Running one while developing the other lets us add capacity in stages, with operating experience informing each step.
"Alongside our construction and infrastructure businesses and our other energy investments, they move the group closer to the long-term recurring income we are building," he added.

Citaglobal New Energy signed a memorandum of understanding with TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd and TIZA AI Sdn Bhd on Nov 16, 2026, to study the feasibility of supplying dedicated off-grid power to the proposed Gebeng AI Data Centre Park and discuss potential commercial arrangements.

80e13d9c6e2c5064: PUTRAJAYA: A total of 77 Malaysian Oil and Gas Services and Equipment (OGSE) companies have generated RM114.82 million in export sales as at Sept 30 this year, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.

Marking five years of implementation, the annual National OGSE Blueprint Forum will be held in Kuala Lumpur on Dec 3, with Akmal Nasrullah scheduled to officiate the event and participate in a panel discussion moderated by Mohd Yazid.
bfaba8147f3d75ab: PETALING JAYA: The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, granted an audience today to Juasseh assemblyman Ismail Lasim, whose resignation as menteri besar was announced last night by Barisan Nasional.

d7f15bb519221fff: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's oil palm industry is well-positioned to meet the requirements of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), backed by a longstanding sustainability framework, mandatory national certification and ongoing efforts to strengthen digital traceability across the supply chain.

The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) in a statement said Malaysia is moving beyond sustainability commitments towards a system that could demonstrate, through verifiable information, where its palm oil comes from, how it is produced and how it moves through the supply chain.

"As the EUDR implementation deadline approaches, Malaysia's priority is to ensure that its established sustainability framework is translated into reliable, accessible and verifiable information that supports operators and exporters in meeting their respective due diligence obligations," it said.

The MPOB noted that the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification scheme was introduced in 2013, with implementation commencing in 2015, reflecting the country's recognition that responsible production and environmental stewardship are fundamental to the industry's long-term competitiveness.

The MSPO 2.0 standard, under MS 2530:2022, provides assurance through independent third-party certification covering legal compliance, environmental protection, traceability, social safeguards and responsible production practices, it said.

Currently, 92.36 per cent of Malaysia's 5.7 million hectares of oil palm planted area has been MSPO-certified, including approximately 181,000 independent smallholders, reflecting the country's commitment to making sustainability a shared responsibility across the industry.

"While MSPO certification does not automatically establish EUDR compliance, it provides important supporting evidence for operators undertaking their due diligence, particularly in demonstrating legal production, responsible land management and sustainability practices," it said.

It added that Malaysia is strengthening digital traceability in the oil palm industry through the development and enhancement of three complementary digital systems, namely GeoSAWIT, e-MSPO, and the Sawit Intelligent Management System (SIMS).
"Moving forward, these three systems will be progressively integrated to establish a more connected digital traceability framework for the Malaysian oil palm industry.

"This integration is intended to link geospatial information, certification records and commercial transaction data, providing a more comprehensive picture of the supply chain, from oil palm production areas and smallholder plots to dealers, mills and other industry operators," it said.

Besides, Malaysia's efforts to align its sustainability framework with international requirements have also received encouraging recognition, such as the Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority.
Meanwhile, MPOB director general Datuk Badrul Hisham Mohd said Malaysia's approach to sustainability goes beyond meeting regulatory requirements.
"We are committed to demonstrating, through credible certification, reliable data and transparent supply chains, that Malaysian palm oil is produced responsibly.
"Equally important, we want to ensure that every segment of the industry, including independent smallholders, can continue to participate in and benefit from international markets," he said.

42b85cf3ad159c56: Amazon Web Services and Blackstone have inked a deal that will see the private equity firm effectively take ownership of two AWS datacenter campuses and then lease them back to the Jeff Bezos outfit under an initial term of 12 years.

Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) says the definitive agreement will see it acquire a 75 percent majority interest in two joint ventures with AWS, in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion.

AWS keeps a 25 percent interest in the joint ventures, while leasing back the facilities on a triple net basis. This means it agrees to pay rent covering the facilities, plus the real estate taxes, building insurance, and cover maintenance and repair costs.

A Form 8-K filed by Blackstone with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) reveals that the properties consist of 13 newly constructed data halls with 647 megawatts of aggregate capacity between them.
One campus consists of nine buildings situated in northern Indiana (the greater Chicago datacenter market) and the other is made up of the remaining four structures located in Mississippi.
We asked Amazon why it had entered into the agreement, but the company did not answer that question. Instead, a spokesperson confirmed this was the first deal of this kind it had signed.

In a supplied remark, VP of AWS Infrastructure Prasad Kalyanaraman said that "Partnering with Blackstone allows us to continue expanding responsibly while keeping communities at the center of how we build."

AWS does lease capacity from other datacenter operators, of course, and has existing agreements with partners like STACK Infrastructure to develop $12 billion worth of campus sites across northwest Louisiana, signed earlier this year.
Sale-leaseback transactions are not unheard of in the datacenter industry. QTS Realty Trust (also backed by Blackstone) developed facilities for lease by Microsoft, for example.
BXDC is a real estate investment trust (REIT), launched by Blackstone on the New York Stock Exchange earlier this year. The AWS deal is its first since then.

"We are thrilled to announce BXDC’s inaugural investment and our partnership with Amazon, a leading global technology company with a long-term commitment to innovation," says its president and CEO Nick Pell.

"The quality, basis and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds. Given the deep expertise across our platform, we believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders."
Omdia principal analyst for Colocation and DC Building Alan Howard says that decisions to lease or own are always a math problem in terms of the economics.

"I'm not sure those datacenter assets bring much benefit to their financials sitting on their balance sheet and it's possible a sale/leaseback is more economical. Keep in mind that all this has nothing to do with all the IT equipment inside, rather just the building and its infrastructure," he told The Register.

"It's also clear that the massive capex spending by hyperscalers is putting pressure on their financials and they are leaning on debt markets to fund some of the buildout. Of course, using debt is not out of the ordinary, but I imagine the debt for AI buildout is significantly more now than in the past."

The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 and is subject to certain closing conditions. According to the Form 8-K, the agreement can be terminated by either party if it isn't closed by December 31, 2026, with the non-breaching party entitled to a termination fee of $150 million. ®

d45665ed2d0b32ad: SINGAPORE: Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hattrick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore in an international friendly on Tuesday.
Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also found the net as the South Americans brushed aside their hosts with a dominant performance at the National Stadium.

Brazil were much changed from their 3-2 loss to Japan on Saturday in which manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were shown red cards, with Vinicius one of only four players retaining their places in the starting line-up.

Bruno Guimaraes took over as skipper and set up the opener after nine minutes, playing a quick pass to Vinicius, who wrong-footed Singapore captain Hariss Harun with his first touch before despatching a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud.
The Real Madrid forward notched his second in the 15th minute after a quick counterattack by the Selecao as Endrick laid the ball off for his unmarked teammate to slot home.
Vinicius was denied by Izwan shortly afterwards, but he completed his hattrick in the 21st minute when he was found completely unmarked in the six-yard box by Estevao's low centre.
Rayan had an effort disallowed for offside, but Endrick added to Brazil's lead in the 31st minute with a low effort from range, which found the bottom right corner.
Estevao also had a goal disallowed for a foul by Vinicius, but the Chelsea winger added to Brazil's tally just after the interval with a deflected shot from the edge of the box.
Rayan rocked the crossbar soon after, but the endeavour of the Bournemouth forward was rewarded in the 65th minute when he rounded substitute goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari to make it 6-0.
Brazil rang the changes in the closing stages, and Allan came off the bench to grab the seventh goal in the 74th minute with a low angled shot which nicked off Raoul Suhaimi on its way into the net.

06a34a4b75b9ef1e: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A policeman whose right wrist was severed in a machete attack by a foreign man in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong, on November 11 is being considered for a field promotion.

Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department (JPJKK) director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail had proposed the promotion in recognition of the officer’s dedication to duty.
“We are processing the necessary documentation through the Selangor Police Contingent.

“We are also looking into other entitlements, including a possible medal award and assistance from several welfare funds,” he told reporters after visiting the officer at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) today.

Also present were Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Bukit Aman JPJKK Deputy Directors Datuk Suryani Sungit and Datuk Nik Ros Azhan Nik Ab Hamid, and Selangor JPJKK chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Mohamad Fakhrudin Abdul Hamid.
On the officer’s condition, Noor Hisam said the 26-year-old Lance Corporal was showing positive progress and was now stable, although he remained in critical condition.

“He is in a general ward but remains under close observation. He is conscious, able to communicate and showing strong determination.
“When I spoke to him earlier, he said he had begun to regain sensation in his fingers, although he had not fully recovered and still needed treatment,” he said.
Noor Hisam said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) was also providing welfare assistance to the officer’s family by bringing his parents from Sarawak to Kuala Lumpur a day after the incident.

db677a9b1374f4d4: KUALA LUMPUR: Teresa Kok (PH-Seputeh) has urged the tourism, arts and culture ministry to turn Visit Malaysia 2026’s sun bear mascots, Wira and Manja, into cartoon characters, soft toys and other merchandise to promote the country overseas.
Kok said the two mascots should have their own animated television series, like the popular animated pair Upin and Ipin, and become internationally recognisable cartoon characters.

The mascots were inspired by the Malayan sun bear, the world’s smallest bear species, which is native to Malaysia. The animals can be seen at the Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre in Sandakan, Sabah.
“We should put our sun bears on par with Kung Fu Panda, Donald Duck, Mickey Mouse, Minnie Mouse, Doraemon and Tom & Jerry,” she said while debating the tourism ministry’s budget in the Dewan Rakyat.

Kok said the mascots had yet to make much of an impression locally, with many people unable to remember their names. She added that some were so unfamiliar with sun bears that a friend had even told her the animal did not exist.

She said the ministry should give the mascots a fresh look to appeal to children and young people. She also showed MPs several designs by UCSI University students, including of sun bears dressed in traditional attire, boxing, dancing and carrying cameras.
Kok said the students' work showed how universities could help the ministry develop new ideas for the mascots.
“Our students are actually very creative. They can help the ministry and Tourism Malaysia come up with new concepts,” she said.
Kok also called on Radio Televisyen Malaysia, Bernama and Media Prima to produce more creative programmes featuring Wira and Manja.

She suggested that the finance ministry allow Tourism Malaysia to sell merchandise based on the two characters, while universities and colleges could be invited to help develop animated shows and other products.
Recalling the first Visit Malaysia Year campaign in 1990, Kok said the orangutan mascot was widely promoted on RTM, while government letterheads also carried the campaign slogan.
She said the widespread publicity helped make the campaign a national effort rather than something left solely to the tourism ministry.

“But we are not seeing that this year. It is as though Visit Malaysia is only a mission for the ministry and Tourism Malaysia,” she said, urging state governments, government agencies and local councils to play a bigger role in promoting the country.

3cb58089f5452487: MANILA, Nov 17 — US President Donald Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday, where thousands of people protested his attendance at a regional summit he will seek to dominate after bruising election losses back home.
The president was greeted by a marching band and honour guard on the tarmac.

Some 13 kilometres (eight miles) away, 2,000 demonstrators faced off with police while carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica”, a reference to a US supply chain initiative that has divided opinions in the Philippines.

The US president was to be immediately flown by helicopter to a meeting of the so-called Quad security alliance, with India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Japan’s Sanae Takaichi and Australia’s Anthony Albanese.

The gathering on the sidelines of the 11-member Association of South-eastt Asian Nations (Asean) summit is the Quad leaders’ first since Trump’s January 2025 return to power, and comes after his Republican party took a drubbing in this month’s midterm elections.

While the Quad – broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence – has quietly progressed in deepening coordination, the short time allotted for Tuesday’s meeting meant it was unlikely to extend beyond pleasantries, Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution told AFP.
The timing, however, carried significance, he said, given the historic meeting Trump will attend with China’s President Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin in just two days.
“It’s a way of inoculating Trump against criticism of caving to authoritarians when he meets with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen,” Hass said.
This would be the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China.

Hayley Channer, economic security director at the Sydney-based United States Studies Centre, said Trump’s decision to include Asean on his travel agenda was noteworthy, as “South-eastt Asia has never been a high priority for the United States”.
Tariffs and chips
Japan’s foreign ministry said the Quad agenda would include discussions of the East and South China Sea – areas where multiple parties have overlapping claims with China.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

US President Donald Trump (back centre) takes part in a Quad leaders’ meeting with Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (front, second left), India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the Solaire Resort on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila on November 17, 2026. — AFP pic
Trump will later attend a meeting with Asean heads of state before going to a gala dinner.
While Asean leaders have spent three days grappling with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with the bloc.
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada’s Mark Carney sang a similar tune on trade, with both explicitly citing a need to wean themselves off dependence on the US market.
Trump’s arrival comes on the heels of an announced US rules shift on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle Asean members.
Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special licence, as the countries were said to represent a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.
Singapore responded by saying it was now exploring ways to facilitate “trusted access” for firms based in the city-state.
Pax Silica
Trump is set to meet with Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to China’s Shenzhen.
Channer, from the US Studies Centre, said the Manila visit was “likely because the US is trying to further its Pax Silica initiative, to build a complete mine-to-chip supply chain”.

Aimed at countering China’s dominance in semiconductors and rare earths, the initiative has been the focus of months of protests in the Philippines, as its flagship 1,620-hectare (about 4,000-acre) AI manufacturing hub north of Manila threatens to displace Indigenous families.

“We are gathered here today to call for the stop of Pax Silica and to save the lands of the Filipino people,” Mariposa, a 21-year-old drag queen, told AFP at Tuesday’s protest while wearing a long black cape emblazoned with the words “Pax Silica Sashay Away!”

c3595f5183833657: KUALA LUMPUR: Health minister Dzulkefly Ahmad has blamed the delay in procuring 989 ambulances on the company appointed to supply the vehicles, saying the firm failed to provide the exact number stipulated in the contract.
